governing_question: After C2 coverage limits and the D5-D10 physical-reduction no-go sequence, which genuinely distinct vadose-zone reduction class still has enough physical authority and SWAP5 compatibility to justify a clean next comparator?

predecessor_evidence.C2: Blind local hydraulic state information is strong, but fail-closed state-domain coverage collapses in asymmetric and rapid-switch histories.
predecessor_evidence.coarse_Richards: R8/R4/R2 provide the current transparent physical-reduction frontier; R2 is the strongest low-resolution structural comparator retained by F-ROMV2.
predecessor_evidence.D5_D8: Instantaneous two-layer Darcy and one/two-segment quasi-steady manifold variants are robust but remain dominated by R2.
predecessor_evidence.D10: The literature-faithful He et al. two-layer fixed-H core is dominated by matched R2 on its supported zero-pressure-head B01 envelope; arbitrary-head extension is not authorized.

scientific_identity: Derived from the same unsaturated Darcy/mass-conservation basis as Richards but reformulated in moisture-content/front coordinates.
Uses finite-water-content finite-volume states and explicit ODE evolution rather than a global nonlinear Richards solve.
Represents infiltration, falling slugs and groundwater-table dynamics with bidirectional exchange.
Published formulation supports homogeneous soil layers and layered profiles, surface flux forcing and moving/fixed water-table interaction.
Mass conservation is a defining numerical property rather than an after-the-fact correction.
evidence: Published analytical/Richards comparisons report very small cumulative infiltration discrepancies in the studied cases even when profile shape differs.
Moving-water-table column experiments show comparable water-content performance to HYDRUS-1D across rising/falling groundwater conditions.
Published SMVE/FMC work reports a vector implementation substantially faster than HYDRUS-1D in its own external benchmark; this is precedent only and not a SWAP5 speed claim.

scientific_identity: Non-iterative sequential vadose-zone approximation designed for regional groundwater models.
Supports bidirectional saturated-unsaturated exchange and dynamic groundwater-table updating.
blockers: The published formulation does not provide the same explicit prescribed lower-boundary control required by the current SWAP development envelope.
Its groundwater-table update uses an empirical soil-specific specific-yield factor whose calibration is scientifically consequential.
Published coarse discretizations can show material cumulative mass residual; finer vertical/time resolution reduces but does not eliminate the governance mismatch.
Root water uptake is not yet part of the core published soil-moisture/flux relation.

scientific_identity: Structure-preserving state aggregation based on clusters of states with similar trajectories.
Supports multiple operating regions and retains physical grouping better than unrestricted POD.
blockers: Published adaptive workflow generates full-order trajectories at operating-region transitions, so the published online route is not a standalone forward accelerator.
Clustering distance threshold and operating-region construction are tuning choices that would need new blind-data governance.
Primary demonstrated value is reduced state-estimation/MHE dimension rather than direct hydrological forward replacement.

scientific_identity: Projection/hyper-reduction can reduce nonlinear evaluation cost and conservative formulations exist in broader finite-volume ROM literature.
blockers: Richards-specific POD evidence does not establish a compelling 1-D forward speed/value case; nonlinear full-state evaluation can erase nominal dimension reduction.
Conservation, physical bounds and OOD fail-closed behavior require substantial intrusive design.
Recent hybrid/deep approaches add training and correction complexity that is not justified before a simpler physics-derived class is tested.

ROM_ASSISTED_FOM.scientific_identity: ROM prediction used as initial guess or solver aid.

selection_basis.statement: D11 does not choose a universal best model. It applies prerequisite filters for the next bounded B01 comparator.
prerequisites: explicit or structurally exact water accounting
online route does not intrinsically require a full-order trajectory
scientifically declared approximation rather than hidden correction
plausible purpose-dependent benefit even when pointwise profile identity is relaxed
clean-room/literature authority can be frozen before SWAP development evidence is consumed
selection_basis.conclusion: FMC/SMVE is the only reviewed remaining class that currently clears all prerequisites strongly enough to justify a new comparator without first changing F-ROMV2 integrity rules.

D12_authority.task: Literature-bound FMC/SMVE equation reconciliation, published benchmark preflight, then a bounded B01 no-sink hydraulic comparator if and only if the preflight closes successfully.
initial_scope: no root extraction or ET in the first SWAP comparison
finite-water-content states with explicit water ledger
groundwater interaction limited to boundary forms directly supported by primary FMC/SMVE authority
development evidence only; existing D/V histories are exposed and cannot become blind confirmation
R16 and admitted R2 remain comparators
required_preflight: reconstruct the published FMC/SMVE equations and sign conventions from primary sources
reproduce at least one published analytical or fixed/moving-water-table benchmark before mapping to SWAP
freeze moisture-bin discretization from literature authority rather than tuning against SWAP outcomes
show exact/explicit mass closure and physically bounded states
prove the selected lower-boundary mapping is within literature authority or label any extension separately before execution
D12_authority.code_provenance: Derive a clean-room research implementation from published equations. Publicly available external code/data may be used only as a secondary oracle after license/provenance review, not copied silently into SWAP5.
D12_authority.runtime_boundary: Published HYDRUS speed ratios are external precedent only. No SWAP5 performance claim until a same-runtime admitted performance experiment exists.
